name: IBPS RRB PO
fullName: IBPS Common Recruitment Process for Regional Rural Banks – Officer Scale I (Assistant Manager)
approxCandidates: ≈6–9 lakh applicants for Officer Scale I (recent cycles, unofficial estimates)
eligibility: Graduate in any discipline; 18–30 years (relaxation for reserved categories); proficiency in the local language of the participating RRB

notification.summary: The CRP RRBs-XV notification was released on 30–31 Aug 2026 with ≈4,256 Officer Scale I vacancies reported (≈13,700 posts across all RRB cadres). Online registration ran from 1 to 21 Sep 2026. The Officer Scale I prelims is scheduled for 21–22 Nov 2026 and the mains for 20 Dec 2026. Dates are from news/education portals; ibps.in could not be reached from the research environment.

pattern.notes: Composite 45-minute paper with no sectional timing; questions are bilingual (Hindi/English). Sectional and overall cut-offs apply and prelims is qualifying only. Mains (200 marks) and an interview (final merit 80:20) follow.

trendAnalysis.summary: RRB PO prelims is a speed test: 80 questions in 45 minutes. Reasoning is easy-to-moderate and puzzle-heavy (4–5 puzzles/seating arrangements, ≈18–22 Qs: floor, box, month, linear with mixed facing, circular), with syllogism, inequality, coding and short miscellaneous questions. Quant is moderate: 2 DI sets (table/bar and caselet, ≈10–12 Qs), quadratic equations, number series (missing and wrong), approximation and arithmetic word problems. Good attempts have usually been 55–65.

pyqBlueprint.method: Compiled from shift-wise memory-based analyses of IBPS RRB Officer Scale-I prelims 2023 (Aug 2023), 2024 (Aug 2024) and 2025 (22–23 Nov 2025) published by coaching sites (Time4Education, Mahendras, Adda247, Physics Wallah), cross-checked with the official IBPS RRB pattern (40 reasoning + 40 quant in 45 minutes). Topic-wise counts for 2025 reasoning were less detailed, so some reasoning archetypes rely mainly on 2023–2024. Patterns are paraphrased; no real question is reproduced.

archetypes.pattern: Table DI (5 rows × 2–3 columns): percentage increase/decrease of one entity between two years, or one entity as a percentage of another
Table DI with a percentage column (e.g. share of a sub-category): compute derived values (sum, average, difference or ratio of derived quantities)
Caselet DI on rural themes (cooperative members, farmers, milk collection): a total split by percentages/fractions, then sub-splits; combine or re-split after a change
Pie-chart DI (shares in % or degrees of a total): find values, differences and ratios across sectors
Bar/line-graph DI (values given for 5–6 categories or months): averages, ratios and percentage differences
Two quadratic equations in x and y with integer/fraction roots; compare x and y using the five standard relations (> ≥ < ≤ / cannot be established)
Missing number series built on differences of squares/cubes, alternate ×n +k, or ×n with increasing n
Wrong number series: one term breaks the ×/+ pattern; find it
Exact simplification with BODMAS, percentages, fractions, squares and square roots; find '?'
Approximation: decimals close to whole numbers in %, ×, ÷, √ and powers; find the nearest value
Find the unknown placed inside the expression (? % of N, √?, ?² or a fraction of ?)
Profit & loss with marked price, discount and cost price (single or successive discounts, 'had he sold for ₹x more')
Percentage word problem: income–expenditure–savings, successive percentage change, or one value as a percentage of another
Partnership with unequal times or a mid-year change of capital; find a partner's share of profit
Ages: present-age ratio with a condition some years before/after; find an age or sum of ages
Ratio & proportion: dividing an amount in a ratio, or changing a ratio by adding/removing a quantity
Time & work / pipes: efficiencies combined, one leaves after some days, or an emptying pipe
Trains crossing poles/platforms/each other, relative speed, or average speed of a round trip
Boats and streams: downstream/upstream speeds and times
Simple vs compound interest: CI–SI difference, amount at CI, or a sum split between two rates
Mixture & alligation: mixing two varieties to a target price/ratio, or adding/replacing liquid
Probability with balls/cards/committees, using combinations
Mensuration: rectangle/circle/cylinder area, perimeter or volume relationships
Linear row (7–9 persons, all facing one direction), sometimes with vacant seats or an attribute; 3–5 questions on positions, neighbours and 'how many between'
Linear arrangement with mixed directions (some face north, some south) or two parallel rows facing each other
Circular table (6–8 persons) facing the centre (or some outside); left/right relations and 'second to the left of' questions
Floor-based puzzle (4–7 floors, sometimes two flats per floor such as flat X/flat Y) with persons and one attribute; 'who lives directly above/below' questions
Scheduling puzzle: persons/events on days of the week or months (sometimes with dates 1xth/2xth); 'how many between' questions
Box stacking: boxes placed one above another, with colour/item attribute and 'how many boxes between' clues
Comparison puzzle: heights/weights/marks of 5–6 persons with 'more than only' clues; ask rank or a derived value
Syllogism with 2–3 statements and two conclusions, including 'possibility' conclusions; standard five options
Syllogism with 'Only a few' or 'No' statements where a definite 'All' conclusion is the trap
Direct inequality: two or three combined statements, two conclusions to check
Inequality where the conclusions form a complementary pair (A > B / A = B) and the answer is 'Either I or II follows'
Blood relation chain or 'pointing to a photograph' statement; gender ambiguity is the usual trap
Coded blood relation: symbols (+, −, ×, ÷ or @, #) denote relations; decode an expression
Direction & distance: a person walks a path with left/right turns; find the shortest distance and direction from start
Point-based direction: several points given relative to each other; find direction/distance between two of them
Letter coding: word coded by letter shifts / reversal / opposite letters; code a new word
Sentence (Chinese) coding: three or four phrases coded in two-letter codes; find the code of a word by elimination
Order & ranking: positions from both ends of a row/class, total count, or persons between two people
Alphanumeric-symbol arrangement: count elements satisfying a 'preceded by / followed by' condition, or find the nth element from an end
English alphabet positions: nth letter from left/right after rearrangement or reversal; letter-pair series
Letter pairs in a word with as many letters between them as in the English alphabet
Meaningful words formed from given letters of a word (each letter used once)
Number formation: digits of 3-digit numbers rearranged/operated on; find the resulting number or difference
Data sufficiency with two statements on seating/coding/blood relation; standard five options
Direction after a sequence of clockwise/anticlockwise turns in degrees

resources.notes: IBPS does not publish RRB question papers or answer keys. Official material is the Information Handout (sample questions) and the online practice test released before the exam on ibps.in, plus pre-exam training for eligible candidates. Previous papers are memory-based compilations by coaching portals.

questions.question:
Six friends A, B, C, D, E and F sit around a circular table, all facing the centre. B sits second to the left of D. E sits immediately to the left of B. A sits opposite B. C is not an immediate neighbour of D.

Who sits immediately to the right of B?
questions.explanation: Clockwise from A: A, D, F, B, E, C (facing the centre, left = clockwise). B's immediate right (anticlockwise) is F.

relevance.note: 6-person circle, unique ADFBEC; RRB PO-level though small

questions.question:
Six friends A, B, C, D, E and F sit around a circular table, all facing the centre. B sits second to the left of D. E sits immediately to the left of B. A sits opposite B. C is not an immediate neighbour of D.

Who sits opposite D?
questions.explanation: Clockwise: A, D, F, B, E, C. D is in seat 2, so the seat opposite (seat 5) has E.

questions.question:
Six friends A, B, C, D, E and F sit around a circular table, all facing the centre. B sits second to the left of D. E sits immediately to the left of B. A sits opposite B. C is not an immediate neighbour of D.

Who are the immediate neighbours of C?
questions.explanation: Clockwise: A, D, F, B, E, C. C sits between E and A.

questions.question:
Six persons P, Q, R, S, T and U sit in a straight row. Some face north and some face south. R sits at one of the extreme ends and faces south. Only two persons sit between R and S. S faces north, and both immediate neighbours of S face the direction opposite to S. R sits immediately to the right of T. U sits at an extreme end and faces north. T faces the same direction as U. P sits immediately to the left of T.

How many persons face south?
questions.explanation: Left to right (west to east): U (N), Q (S), S (N), P (S), T (N), R (S). Q, P and R face south — three.

questions.question:
Six persons P, Q, R, S, T and U sit in a straight row. Some face north and some face south. R sits at one of the extreme ends and faces south. Only two persons sit between R and S. S faces north, and both immediate neighbours of S face the direction opposite to S. R sits immediately to the right of T. U sits at an extreme end and faces north. T faces the same direction as U. P sits immediately to the left of T.

Who sits immediately to the right of Q?
questions.explanation: Row (west→east): U (N), Q (S), S (N), P (S), T (N), R (S). Q faces south, so his right is towards the west — U.

relevance.note: Right of south-facing Q = U; orientation trap

questions.question:
Six persons P, Q, R, S, T and U sit in a straight row. Some face north and some face south. R sits at one of the extreme ends and faces south. Only two persons sit between R and S. S faces north, and both immediate neighbours of S face the direction opposite to S. R sits immediately to the right of T. U sits at an extreme end and faces north. T faces the same direction as U. P sits immediately to the left of T.

Who sits between S and T?
questions.explanation: Row (west→east): U, Q, S, P, T, R. P sits between S and T.

questions.question:
Six persons G, H, I, J, K and L travel in six different months from January to June of the same year (one person per month), each to a different city — Delhi, Pune, Agra, Goa, Ooty and Leh. G travels in a month that has 31 days. H travels in the month immediately before G, and L travels in the month immediately after G. L goes to Delhi. Only one person travels between G and the one who goes to Agra, who travels after G. I travels in June. The one who goes to Goa travels in January and the one who goes to Ooty travels in June. K travels before J. H does not go to Pune. I does not go to Leh. J does not go to Ooty.

Who goes to Agra?
questions.explanation: G must be in March (January leaves no month for H; May would put L in June, which is I's). So H Feb, L Apr (Delhi), Agra in May. K before J gives K Jan (Goa), J May (Agra).

questions.question:
Six persons G, H, I, J, K and L travel in six different months from January to June of the same year (one person per month), each to a different city — Delhi, Pune, Agra, Goa, Ooty and Leh. G travels in a month that has 31 days. H travels in the month immediately before G, and L travels in the month immediately after G. L goes to Delhi. Only one person travels between G and the one who goes to Agra, who travels after G. I travels in June. The one who goes to Goa travels in January and the one who goes to Ooty travels in June. K travels before J. H does not go to Pune. I does not go to Leh. J does not go to Ooty.

In which month does H travel?
questions.explanation: G travels in March, so H (immediately before G) travels in February.

questions.question:
Six persons G, H, I, J, K and L travel in six different months from January to June of the same year (one person per month), each to a different city — Delhi, Pune, Agra, Goa, Ooty and Leh. G travels in a month that has 31 days. H travels in the month immediately before G, and L travels in the month immediately after G. L goes to Delhi. Only one person travels between G and the one who goes to Agra, who travels after G. I travels in June. The one who goes to Goa travels in January and the one who goes to Ooty travels in June. K travels before J. H does not go to Pune. I does not go to Leh. J does not go to Ooty.

How many persons travel between K and L?
questions.explanation: Order: K (Jan, Goa), H (Feb, Leh), G (Mar, Pune), L (Apr, Delhi), J (May, Agra), I (Jun, Ooty). Between K and L: H and G — two.

questions.question:
Seven boxes M, N, O, P, Q, R and S are kept one above another (position 1 is the bottom, 7 the top). Q is exactly in the middle of the stack. Only two boxes are between Q and P, and P is above Q. N is immediately below R, and R is above Q. Only one box is between M and N. S is above O.

Which box is placed second from the bottom?
questions.explanation: Bottom to top: O, S, M, Q, N, R, P. S is second from the bottom.

questions.question:
Seven boxes M, N, O, P, Q, R and S are kept one above another (position 1 is the bottom, 7 the top). Q is exactly in the middle of the stack. Only two boxes are between Q and P, and P is above Q. N is immediately below R, and R is above Q. Only one box is between M and N. S is above O.

How many boxes are between O and N?
questions.explanation: Bottom to top: O, S, M, Q, N, R, P. Between O (1) and N (5) are S, M and Q — three.

questions.question:
Seven boxes M, N, O, P, Q, R and S are kept one above another (position 1 is the bottom, 7 the top). Q is exactly in the middle of the stack. Only two boxes are between Q and P, and P is above Q. N is immediately below R, and R is above Q. Only one box is between M and N. S is above O.

Which box is placed immediately above Q?
questions.explanation: Q = 4, P = 7; N–R must be 5–6, so N is immediately above Q. M is 3 (two from N), and O, S take 1, 2.

questions.question: Five students A, B, C, D and E scored different marks. B scored more than only two students. D scored more than B but less than A. E scored less than C. Who scored the second lowest marks?
questions.explanation: B is third from the top; A > D > B are the top three, and C > E are below B. Order: A, D, B, C, E — C is second lowest.

questions.question: Four persons P, Q, R and S sit around a square table, one on each side, facing the centre. Q sits to the immediate right of P. S does not sit opposite Q. Who sits to the immediate left of P?
questions.explanation: S is not opposite Q, so S is opposite P, and R is opposite Q. Q is on P's right, so R is on P's left.

questions.question: Five persons V, W, X, Y and Z live on different floors of a five-storey building (floor 1 is the bottom). V lives on an even-numbered floor. W lives immediately above V. X lives on the top floor. Y lives on a floor below Z. Who lives on floor 4?
questions.explanation: X is on 5. V on 4 would put W on 5 (X's), so V = 2 and W = 3. Floors 1 and 4 remain; Y below Z → Y = 1, Z = 4.

questions.question:
Statements: Some boxes are cartons. All cartons are bags.
Conclusions: I. Some boxes are bags. II. Some bags are cartons.
questions.explanation: Boxes that are cartons are bags (I). Since all cartons are bags, some bags are cartons (II). Both follow.

questions.question:
Statements: No car is a bus. All buses are trucks. Some trucks are vans.
Conclusions: I. Some trucks are not cars. II. All vans being cars is a possibility.
questions.explanation: Buses are trucks and no bus is a car, so some trucks are not cars (I). Vans are only linked to trucks; nothing stops all vans from being cars (II is possible). Both follow.

relevance.note: No/All/Some with possibility conclusion; good RRB trap

questions.question:
Statement: W > X ≥ Y > Z
Conclusions: I. W > Z  II. Y ≥ W
questions.explanation: W > X ≥ Y > Z gives W > Z; and W > Y, so II is false. Only I follows.

questions.question:
Statements: G ≤ H < I; J > I; K ≥ J
Conclusions: I. K > G  II. H < J
questions.explanation: K ≥ J > I > H ≥ G gives K > G and H < J. Both follow.

questions.question: If 'CLOUD' is written as 'DMPVE' in a code, how is 'RAIN' written?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward: R→S, A→B, I→J, N→O = SBJO.

questions.question: In a code, 'WATER' is written as 'XZUDS'. How is 'FIELD' written in that code?
questions.explanation: Letters move +1, −1 alternately: W+1, A−1, T+1, E−1, R+1. FIELD → F+1 = G, I−1 = H, E+1 = F, L−1 = K, D+1 = E = GHFKE.

questions.question: M is the sister of N. N is the son of O. O is the wife of P. Q is the brother of P. How is M related to Q?
questions.explanation: M and N are children of P and O. Q is P's brother, so M is Q's niece.

questions.question: A + B means A is the father of B; A − B means A is the wife of B; A × B means A is the brother of B; A ÷ B means A is the daughter of B. If P × Q + R − S, how is Q related to S?
questions.explanation: Q + R: Q is R's father. R − S: R is S's wife. So Q is the father of S's wife — S's father-in-law.

relevance.note: Symbol-coded relation to father-in-law; R16 faithful

questions.question: Raj is facing east. He turns 135° anticlockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation: East → 90° anticlockwise = North → a further 45° = North-West.

questions.question: A is 10 m north of B. C is 6 m east of B. D is 10 m north of C. How far and in which direction is D from A?
In a row of girls, Rita is 13th from the left and Monika is 17th from the right. When they interchange positions, Rita becomes 22nd from the left. How many girls are in the row?
questions.explanation: Rita's new place is Monika's old place: 22nd from the left and 17th from the right. Total = 22 + 17 − 1 = 38.

questions.question: Which letter is 5th to the left of the 9th letter from the right end of the English alphabet (A to Z)?
questions.explanation: 9th from the right = 27 − 9 = 18th letter = R. 5th to its left = 13th letter = M.

relevance.note: Alphabet position from right then left

questions.question:
Arrangement: B 3 D @ 6 F H 2 # J 8 K % L 5 M
How many letters are immediately preceded by a number and immediately followed by a symbol?
questions.explanation: D (3 D @) and K (8 K %) qualify; F is followed by H and M has nothing after it. Two.

relevance.note: Letters between number and symbol count

questions.question:
Numbers: 739 482 615 924 368
If the digits of each number are arranged in ascending order within the number, which original number will become the second largest?
questions.explanation: New numbers: 379, 248, 156, 249, 368. In descending order: 379, 368, 249, 248, 156. The second largest, 368, comes from 368.

questions.question:
How is J related to K?
I. J is the brother of L, who is the daughter of K.
II. K is the wife of M, who is the father of J.
options: The data in statement I alone are sufficient, but the data in statement II alone are not
The data in statement II alone are sufficient, but the data in statement I alone are not
The data in either statement I alone or statement II alone are sufficient
The data in both statements I and II together are not sufficient
The data in both statements I and II together are necessary
questions.explanation: From I: L is K's daughter and J is L's brother, so J is K's son — sufficient. From II: K is J's mother, but J's gender is unknown (son or daughter) — not sufficient.

questions.question:
The table shows the number of farmers (in hundreds) who took crop loans from five RRB branches in 2025 and the percentage of them who were women.
Branch | Farmers | Women %
A | 40 | 30%
B | 55 | 20%
C | 48 | 25%
D | 60 | 35%
E | 45 | 40%

How many women farmers took crop loans from branch D?
questions.explanation: 35% of 60 hundred = 21 hundred = 2,100.

The table shows the number of farmers (in hundreds) who took crop loans from five RRB branches in 2025 and the percentage of them who were women.
Branch | Farmers | Women %
A | 40 | 30%
B | 55 | 20%

If in 2026 the number of farmers at branch B rises by 20% and the share of women becomes 30%, by how many will the number of women farmers at B increase over 2025?
questions.explanation: 2025: 20% of 55 = 11 hundred. 2026: 66 × 30% = 19.8 hundred. Increase = 8.8 hundred = 880.

relevance.note: Projected change with new %; good derived question

questions.question:
A dairy cooperative collected 12,000 litres of milk in a week from three villages X, Y and Z. X supplied 40% of the total, and Y supplied 1,200 litres more than Z. The cooperative pays ₹40 per litre to X, ₹38 per litre to Y and ₹42 per litre to Z.

How many litres of milk did village Y supply?

relevance.note: Milk cooperative caselet, RRB rural theme

questions.question: 60% of a number is 48 more than 40% of the same number. What is the number?
questions.explanation: 20% of the number = 48 → number = 240.

questions.question: An article marked at ₹2,500 is sold after two successive discounts of 20% and 10%. What is the selling price?
A dishonest dealer claims to sell goods at cost price but uses a 900 g weight in place of 1 kg. What is his profit percentage?
questions.explanation: He gives 900 g for the price of 1000 g: profit = 100/900 × 100 = 11 1/9%.

questions.question: ₹7,800 is divided among A, B and C in the ratio 1/2 : 1/3 : 1/4. What is C's share?
A mother is now three times as old as her daughter. Eight years from now she will be twice as old as her daughter. What is the mother's present age?
questions.explanation: 3D + 8 = 2(D + 8) → D = 8, mother = 24 years.

questions.question: A is twice as efficient as B. Together they finish a job in 18 days. In how many days can A alone finish it?
questions.explanation: Let B do b per day, A 2b: 3b = 1/18 → b = 1/54, A = 1/27 → 27 days.

questions.question: A boat's speed in still water is 15 km/h and the stream flows at 3 km/h. How long will it take to go 36 km downstream and return to the starting point?
questions.explanation: Downstream 36/18 = 2 h; upstream 36/12 = 3 h. Total 5 h.

questions.question: A train crosses a 200 m platform in 20 seconds and a 400 m bridge in 30 seconds. What is the length of the train?
A sum of money doubles itself in 5 years at compound interest. In how many years will it become 8 times itself at the same rate?
questions.explanation: 8 = 2³, so it takes 3 × 5 = 15 years.

questions.question: In what ratio must rice costing ₹40/kg be mixed with rice costing ₹55/kg so that the mixture is worth ₹45/kg?
The perimeter of a rectangle is 56 m and its length is 4 m more than its breadth. What is its area?

Eight persons A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H live in a four-storey building (floor 1 is the lowest and floor 4 the topmost). Each floor has two flats — flat X on the west and flat Y on the east — and flat X of every floor is directly above flat X of the floor below it (similarly for flat Y). Each flat has exactly one person.
A lives in flat X on an even-numbered floor. F lives on the same floor as A. D lives immediately above A in the same type of flat. C lives in flat Y on an odd-numbered floor below F's floor. H lives immediately below B in the same type of flat. E lives below G.

Who lives in flat X of floor 4?
questions.explanation: Floor 4: G (X), B (Y); floor 3: D (X), H (Y); floor 2: A (X), F (Y); floor 1: E (X), C (Y). G lives in flat X of floor 4.

relevance.note: 4-floor two-flat puzzle, unique; RRB R04 faithful

questions.question:
Eight persons A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H live in a four-storey building (floor 1 is the lowest and floor 4 the topmost). Each floor has two flats — flat X on the west and flat Y on the east — and flat X of every floor is directly above flat X of the floor below it (similarly for flat Y). Each flat has exactly one person.
A lives in flat X on an even-numbered floor. F lives on the same floor as A. D lives immediately above A in the same type of flat. C lives in flat Y on an odd-numbered floor below F's floor. H lives immediately below B in the same type of flat. E lives below G.

Who lives on the same floor as H?
questions.explanation: Floor 4: G (X), B (Y); floor 3: D (X), H (Y); floor 2: A (X), F (Y); floor 1: E (X), C (Y). D shares floor 3 with H.

questions.question:
Eight persons A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H live in a four-storey building (floor 1 is the lowest and floor 4 the topmost). Each floor has two flats — flat X on the west and flat Y on the east — and flat X of every floor is directly above flat X of the floor below it (similarly for flat Y). Each flat has exactly one person.
A lives in flat X on an even-numbered floor. F lives on the same floor as A. D lives immediately above A in the same type of flat. C lives in flat Y on an odd-numbered floor below F's floor. H lives immediately below B in the same type of flat. E lives below G.

Who lives immediately below D?
questions.explanation: Floor 4: G (X), B (Y); floor 3: D (X), H (Y); floor 2: A (X), F (Y); floor 1: E (X), C (Y). A lives in flat X of floor 2, directly below D.

questions.question:
Eight persons A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H live in a four-storey building (floor 1 is the lowest and floor 4 the topmost). Each floor has two flats — flat X on the west and flat Y on the east — and flat X of every floor is directly above flat X of the floor below it (similarly for flat Y). Each flat has exactly one person.
A lives in flat X on an even-numbered floor. F lives on the same floor as A. D lives immediately above A in the same type of flat. C lives in flat Y on an odd-numbered floor below F's floor. H lives immediately below B in the same type of flat. E lives below G.

How many persons live above C in flat Y?
questions.explanation: Floor 4: G (X), B (Y); floor 3: D (X), H (Y); floor 2: A (X), F (Y); floor 1: E (X), C (Y). F, H and B live in flat Y above C — three persons.

relevance.note: Persons above C in flat Y = 3

questions.question:
Eight persons J, K, L, M, N, O, P and Q sit in a straight row from west to east. Some of them face north and some face south.
J sits third from the west end and faces north. K sits second to the right of J and faces south. P sits immediately to the left of K and faces the same direction as J. L sits second to the right of P and faces south. N sits immediately to the right of L. M sits at one of the extreme ends. Q is an immediate neighbour of M. The persons sitting at the two extreme ends face opposite directions. Q faces the direction opposite to M. O faces the same direction as P, while N faces the direction opposite to O.

How many persons face south?
questions.explanation: West to east: M (N), Q (S), J (N), O (N), K (S), P (N), N (S), L (S). Q, K, N and L face south.

questions.question:
Eight persons J, K, L, M, N, O, P and Q sit in a straight row from west to east. Some of them face north and some face south.
J sits third from the west end and faces north. K sits second to the right of J and faces south. P sits immediately to the left of K and faces the same direction as J. L sits second to the right of P and faces south. N sits immediately to the right of L. M sits at one of the extreme ends. Q is an immediate neighbour of M. The persons sitting at the two extreme ends face opposite directions. Q faces the direction opposite to M. O faces the same direction as P, while N faces the direction opposite to O.

Who sits second to the left of O?
questions.explanation: West to east: M (N), Q (S), J (N), O (N), K (S), P (N), N (S), L (S). O faces north, so its left is west: J, then Q — Q is second to the left of O.

questions.question:

Who sits immediately to the right of N?
questions.explanation: West to east: M (N), Q (S), J (N), O (N), K (S), P (N), N (S), L (S). N faces south, so its right is west: P.

questions.question:
Eight persons J, K, L, M, N, O, P and Q sit in a straight row from west to east. Some of them face north and some face south.

Which of the following pairs sits at the two extreme ends of the row?
questions.explanation: West to east: M (N), Q (S), J (N), O (N), K (S), P (N), N (S), L (S). M (west end) and L (east end).

questions.question:
Eight persons A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H have meetings on four days of a week — Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday. On each of these days there are two meetings, one in the morning and one in the evening, and each person has exactly one meeting.
B has a meeting in the morning on a day after Tuesday. Only two meetings are held between B's meeting and D's meeting, and D's meeting is after B's. G has a meeting on the same day as B. E has a meeting immediately before D. A has a meeting in the evening, and only two meetings are held between A's meeting and E's meeting. F has a meeting on the same day as A. C has a meeting before H.

Who has a meeting on Thursday evening?
questions.explanation: Mon: C (morning), H (evening); Tue: F, A; Thu: B, G; Fri: E, D. G has the Thursday evening meeting.

questions.question:
Eight persons A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H have meetings on four days of a week — Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday. On each of these days there are two meetings, one in the morning and one in the evening, and each person has exactly one meeting.
B has a meeting in the morning on a day after Tuesday. Only two meetings are held between B's meeting and D's meeting, and D's meeting is after B's. G has a meeting on the same day as B. E has a meeting immediately before D. A has a meeting in the evening, and only two meetings are held between A's meeting and E's meeting. F has a meeting on the same day as A. C has a meeting before H.

How many meetings are held between F's meeting and G's meeting?
questions.explanation: Mon: C (morning), H (evening); Tue: F, A; Thu: B, G; Fri: E, D. A (Tue evening) and B (Thu morning) lie between F and G.

questions.question:

Who has a meeting on the same day as H?
questions.explanation: Mon: C (morning), H (evening); Tue: F, A; Thu: B, G; Fri: E, D. C and H both have meetings on Monday.

questions.question:
Eight persons A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H have meetings on four days of a week — Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday. On each of these days there are two meetings, one in the morning and one in the evening, and each person has exactly one meeting.

C has a meeting before H.

Whose meeting is held immediately after A's meeting?
questions.explanation: Mon: C (morning), H (evening); Tue: F, A; Thu: B, G; Fri: E, D. After Tuesday evening (A) comes Thursday morning (B).

questions.question:
Eight persons A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H sit around a circular table, all facing away from the centre.
B sits third to the right of A. F sits immediately to the right of B. H sits second to the left of A. C is an immediate neighbour of both F and H. E is not an immediate neighbour of B. D sits second to the left of B.

Who sits exactly opposite G?
questions.explanation: Clockwise from A: A, D, G, B, F, C, H, E. For persons facing away from the centre, right is clockwise. Opposite G (4 seats away) is H.

questions.question:
Eight persons A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H sit around a circular table, all facing away from the centre.
B sits third to the right of A. F sits immediately to the right of B. H sits second to the left of A. C is an immediate neighbour of both F and H. E is not an immediate neighbour of B. D sits second to the left of B.

Who sits second to the right of H?
questions.explanation: Clockwise from A: A, D, G, B, F, C, H, E. For persons facing away from the centre, right is clockwise. Moving clockwise from H: E, A — A is second to the right of H.

questions.question:
Eight persons A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H sit around a circular table, all facing away from the centre.
B sits third to the right of A. F sits immediately to the right of B. H sits second to the left of A. C is an immediate neighbour of both F and H. E is not an immediate neighbour of B. D sits second to the left of B.

How many persons sit between D and C when counted clockwise from D?
questions.explanation: Clockwise from A: A, D, G, B, F, C, H, E. For persons facing away from the centre, right is clockwise. Clockwise from D: G, B, F, then C — three persons in between.

questions.question:
Statements: All books are pages. Some pages are covers. No cover is a pen.
Conclusions: I. Some pages are not pens. II. Some books are covers.
questions.explanation: The pages that are covers cannot be pens, so I follows. Books and covers have no definite link, so II does not follow.

questions.question:
Statements: Only a few rings are bands. No band is a chain.
Conclusions: I. All chains can be rings. II. Some bands are rings.
questions.explanation: 'Only a few rings are bands' gives some rings are bands, so some bands are rings (II follows). The rings that are not bands may all be chains — nothing forbids all chains being rings, so I is a valid possibility. Both follow.

questions.question:
Statements: P > Q ≥ R; S < R ≤ T; U ≥ T
Conclusions: I. Q > T  II. U > S
questions.explanation: Q ≥ R ≤ T gives no relation between Q and T, so I does not follow. U ≥ T ≥ R > S gives U > S, so II follows.

questions.question:
Statements: A ≥ B > C ≥ D; E < D
Conclusions: I. C > D  II. C = D
questions.explanation: C ≥ D, so either C > D or C = D. Neither alone is certain, but one of them must be true: Either I or II follows.

questions.question: In a certain code, 'FARM' is written as 'HCTO'. How is 'SEED' written in that code?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves two places forward: S → U, E → G, E → G, D → F. SEED → UGGF.

questions.question: In a code language, 'grow more crops' is written as 'ti la ro', 'crops need water' is written as 'ro mi ka' and 'more water daily' is written as 'ka la su'. What is the code for 'need'?
questions.explanation: crops = ro (sentences 1 and 2), more = la (1 and 3), water = ka (2 and 3). The remaining code in sentence 2, 'mi', means 'need'.

questions.question: Introducing a woman, Suresh said, 'She is the wife of the only son of my father's father.' How is the woman related to Suresh?
questions.explanation: The only son of Suresh's paternal grandfather is Suresh's father; his wife is Suresh's mother.

questions.question:
In a certain code, 'A $ B' means A is the son of B; 'A # B' means A is the sister of B; 'A * B' means A is the husband of B; and 'A @ B' means A is the mother of B.
If P # Q $ R * S, how is P related to S?
questions.explanation: Q $ R: Q is R's son. R * S: R is S's husband, so S is Q's mother. P # Q: P is Q's sister, so P is S's daughter.

questions.question: A man is facing west. He turns 45° clockwise, then 180° anticlockwise and then 90° clockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation: West → 45° clockwise = North-West → 180° anticlockwise = South-East → 90° clockwise = South-West.

questions.question: Kavita walks 5 km towards the south, turns east and walks 3 km, turns north and walks 9 km, and then turns west and walks 3 km. How far and in which direction is she from her starting point?
questions.explanation: East–west movements cancel (3 km each way). North 9 − south 5 = 4 km north of the start.

questions.question: In a row of children, A is 7th from the left end and B is 11th from the right end. When A and B interchange their positions, A becomes 15th from the left end. How many children are there in the row?
questions.explanation: After the swap A takes B's place, which is 15th from the left and 11th from the right. Total = 15 + 11 − 1 = 25.

questions.question:
Study the arrangement:
W 3 # E 8 @ K 1 L $ 6 R % 9 T 2 & P
If all the symbols are removed from the arrangement, which element will be 6th from the right end?
questions.explanation: Without symbols: W 3 E 8 K 1 L 6 R 9 T 2 P. Counting from the right: P, 2, T, 9, R, 6 — the 6th is 6.

questions.question:
Numbers: 472  815  369  624  953
If the digits of each number are arranged in descending order within the number, what is the sum of the digits of the second smallest number so formed?
questions.explanation: New numbers: 742, 851, 963, 642, 953. In ascending order: 642, 742, 851, 953, 963. The second smallest is 742, whose digit sum is 13.

questions.question: If a meaningful English word can be formed using the 2nd, 4th, 5th and 7th letters of the word 'PLANETS' (each letter used once), what is the third letter of that word? If no word can be formed, answer X; if more than one word can be formed, answer Z.
questions.explanation: The letters are L, N, E and S, which form only 'LENS'. Its third letter is N.

questions.question:
On which day of the week did Meena visit the bank?
I. Meena visited the bank after Monday but before Thursday.
II. Meena did not visit the bank on Wednesday, and she visited it on a day after Monday.
options: The data in statement I alone are sufficient, but the data in statement II alone are not
The data in statement II alone are sufficient, but the data in statement I alone are not
The data in either statement I alone or statement II alone are sufficient
The data in both statements I and II together are not sufficient
The data in both statements I and II together are necessary
questions.explanation: I alone leaves Tuesday or Wednesday. II alone leaves Tuesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday or Sunday. Together only Tuesday remains, so both statements are needed.

questions.question:
A village cooperative has 600 members: 45% are farmers, 30% are artisans and the rest are traders. Two-thirds of the farmers, 40% of the artisans and 60% of the traders have taken loans from the cooperative.

How many members have taken loans?
questions.explanation: Farmers 270 → 180 loans; artisans 180 → 72; traders 150 → 90. Total = 342.

questions.question:
A village cooperative has 600 members: 45% are farmers, 30% are artisans and the rest are traders. Two-thirds of the farmers, 40% of the artisans and 60% of the traders have taken loans from the cooperative.

Members without loans form what percentage of all members?

A village cooperative has 600 members: 45% are farmers, 30% are artisans and the rest are traders. Two-thirds of the farmers, 40% of the artisans and 60% of the traders have taken loans from the cooperative.

What is the ratio of farmers without loans to traders without loans?
questions.explanation: Farmers without loans = 270 − 180 = 90; traders without loans = 150 − 90 = 60. 90 : 60 = 3 : 2.

questions.question:
A village cooperative has 600 members: 45% are farmers, 30% are artisans and the rest are traders. Two-thirds of the farmers, 40% of the artisans and 60% of the traders have taken loans from the cooperative.

If 20 new artisans join the cooperative and all of them take loans, what percentage of the artisans will then have loans?
questions.explanation: Artisans become 200, with loans 72 + 20 = 92. 92/200 × 100 = 46%.

29.97 × 13.02 + 47.89% of 1,250.3 ≈ ?
Find the next term: 9, 10, 14, 23, 39, ?
questions.explanation: Differences 1², 2², 3², 4², so next is 39 + 5² = 64.

questions.question: Find the next term: 3, 7, 23, 95, 479, ?
Find the next term: 2, 5, 14, 41, 122, ?
questions.explanation: Each term = previous × 3 − 1: 122 × 3 − 1 = 365.

questions.question: Find the wrong number in the series: 10, 12, 16, 24, 40, 74
questions.explanation: Differences should double: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 → 10, 12, 16, 24, 40, 72. 74 is wrong.

questions.question:
Solve and compare.
I. x² + 9x + 20 = 0
II. y² + 5y + 6 = 0
options: x = y or the relationship cannot be established
questions.explanation: I: (x + 4)(x + 5) = 0 → x = −4, −5. II: (y + 2)(y + 3) = 0 → y = −2, −3. Every x is less than every y: x < y.

questions.question:
Solve and compare.
I. x² − 16 = 0
II. y² − 9y + 20 = 0
options: x = y or the relationship cannot be established
questions.explanation: I: x = 4 or −4. II: (y − 4)(y − 5) = 0 → y = 4, 5. x is never greater than y and equals y when both are 4: x ≤ y.

relevance.note: Pure square x=+-4 with y root 4 -> x<=y

questions.question:
Solve and compare.
I. 2x² − 13x + 21 = 0
II. 3y² − 7y + 2 = 0
options: x = y or the relationship cannot be established
questions.explanation: I: (2x − 7)(x − 3) = 0 → x = 3.5, 3. II: (3y − 1)(y − 2) = 0 → y = 1/3, 2. Every x is greater than every y: x > y.

questions.question: A shopkeeper sells an article at a profit of 20%. Had he bought it 10% cheaper and sold it for ₹18 less, he would have gained 25%. What is the cost price of the article?
An article marked at ₹1,600 is sold at a discount of 15%, and the seller still makes a profit of 13⅓%. What is the cost price?
The population of a village is 20,000. It increases by 10% in the first year and decreases by 10% in the second year. What will the population be after two years?
A and B start a business with capitals in the ratio 3 : 5. After 4 months A doubles his capital, while B keeps his unchanged. What is the ratio of their profits at the end of the year?
The sum of the present ages of A and B is 54 years. Six years ago their ages were in the ratio 2 : 5. What is B's present age?
questions.explanation: Six years ago the sum was 54 − 12 = 42 = 7k → k = 6. B then = 30, so B now = 36 years.

questions.question: A and B can do a piece of work in 12 days, B and C in 15 days, and C and A in 20 days. In how many days can A alone do it?
Two trains 150 m and 100 m long run on parallel tracks in the same direction at 72 km/h and 54 km/h. How long will the faster train take to cross the slower one completely?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 72 − 54 = 18 km/h = 5 m/s. Distance = 150 + 100 = 250 m. Time = 50 s. (10 s wrongly adds the speeds.)

questions.question: A boat covers 40 km downstream in 2 hours and the same distance upstream in 4 hours. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
questions.explanation: Downstream 20 km/h, upstream 10 km/h. Still-water speed = (20 + 10)/2 = 15 km/h.

questions.question: The compound interest on a sum for 2 years at 10% per annum, compounded annually, is ₹525. What is the simple interest on the same sum for the same period at the same rate?
A container holds 60 litres of milk. 6 litres are taken out and replaced with water, and this process is repeated once more. How much milk is now left in the container?
questions.explanation: Milk left = 60 × (1 − 6/60)² = 60 × 0.81 = 48.6 litres. (48 litres assumes pure milk is removed both times.)

questions.question: The area of a circle is 154 cm². What is its circumference? (Take π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: πr² = 154 → r² = 49 → r = 7 cm. Circumference = 2 × 22/7 × 7 = 44 cm.
